_doc: Pass 130 (lane LE): the Trail tab's hint box (trail_hint.js). One entry per upgrade type of game/content/trail/trail.json: `what` = what the type does in play, in a designer's words; `note` = optional, what is easy to get wrong (never shown to the player). Tools only: the game never reads this file. A type without an entry falls back to its `text`; selftest_P130LE.py fails when a type in trail.json has none. Written from the code as of pass 130 (StatSheet.PLAYER_DEFAULTS, WeaponInstance.rebuild, Player.gd, PickupManager.drop_from, CardPool, MirrorDanger.gd): when a stat's rule changes, change its words here.

might.what: Every weapon hits harder. All the Trail's Might adds up into one multiplier on each weapon's damage (+5% and +8% make x1.13), which then multiplies with what Cards and items give.
might.note: The plainest power on the Trail: every build gains from it the same.

tempo.what: Every weapon fires sooner. It cuts each weapon's cooldown by this share: 0.04 = cooldown x0.96, about 4.2% more shots.
tempo.note: The player reads "Attack speed +4%" but it is a cooldown cut (stat `cooldown`, per -1): the gain in shots grows faster than the number (a 50% sum doubles the shots). A weapon's cooldown never goes under 0.05 s.

area.what: Every weapon reaches wider: blasts, cones, beams, patches and orbits are this much bigger.
area.note: Worth little to a weapon that fires single rounds.

shot_speed.what: Rounds fly faster. Only speed: no more damage, no more range.
shot_speed.note: Nothing for weapons without a flying round (beams, breath, orbiters).

duration.what: What a weapon leaves or holds lasts longer: pools, patches, turrets, beams, a spin's time.
duration.note: Not burns, poison and slows on creatures (that is Tight Grip), and not power-ups (that is Slow Sip).

amount.what: Every weapon fires one more projectile each time it attacks (for a weapon that counts bounces, one more bounce).
amount.note: A whole number. By far the strongest type per node: every weapon in the build gains a whole extra shot.

crit_chance.what: The chance a hit is critical, added to the outlaw's 1%: 0.05 = five more hits in a hundred.
crit_chance.note: Added, not multiplied: +5% is five points.

crit_damage.what: How hard a critical hit lands, added to the base x2: 0.25 = a crit deals x2.25.

big_game.what: More damage to bosses, Elites and the big creature kinds: 0.15 = x1.15 against them. The regular crowd takes the same as before.
big_game.note: It shortens boss fights only; a boss's HP also grows with the outlaw's recent DPS.

grip.what: Burns, poison, slows, marks and pins that the outlaw's side puts on creatures last this much longer.
grip.note: Only what sits on creatures. Buffs on the outlaw and weapon effects (Long Fuse) are not changed.

health.what: More max health: 0.10 = 10% on top (an outlaw starts from 100 before Cards and items).
health.note: All the Trail's Grit adds into one multiplier, which multiplies with other sources.

plate.what: Every hit the outlaw takes is cut by this share: 0.06 = 6% less damage from everything.
plate.note: Added to other reduction; the game caps the total at 80%.

regen.what: Health points restored every second, a flat number (0.6 = 0.6 HP a second). It pauses for about 3 seconds after a hit.
regen.note: Flat, not a percent: weak beside big max health. Tonic makes it bigger.

tonic.what: Every heal on the outlaw is this much bigger: regen, life steal, cake, structures.
tonic.note: Nothing by itself: it needs a source of healing.

evade.what: The chance a hit misses outright: no damage and no shove.
evade.note: Added, in points (0.05 = five hits in a hundred). The code caps it at 90%.

shield.what: A shield of this many points on top of health. It takes the hits first and comes back after 3 seconds without a hit, half of it a second.
shield.note: Flat points (25 = a quarter of a fresh outlaw's health).

second_wind.what: The share of max health the outlaw stands up with after a revive, added to the base 40%: 0.15 = up at 55%.
second_wind.note: Only matters when a revive is used. Past 100% in all, the rest buys untouchable seconds instead (10 s for each 100%).

extra_life.what: One more revive in every run on the Down! screen (every outlaw has one already).

boots.what: The outlaw walks faster: 0.03 = 3% on his 3.6 m/s.
boots.note: Speed is safety and gem collection; creatures' far speed is set by the map, not by this.

magnet.what: The reach in which gems and coins fly to the outlaw (1.5 m at the start) is this much wider.

luck.what: Luck lifts the rarer cards at a level-up (uncommon by half the number, rare by it, epic x1.5, legendary x2), makes creatures drop coins more often (x 1 + luck) and adds a little to medium gems and to an Elite's vacuum.
luck.note: Added, starting from 0: 0.10 = 10% more coin drops and legendary cards 20% more likely by weight.

greed.what: Coins gained in a run are worth this much more.
greed.note: It speeds the whole Trail up: every node bought after it comes sooner.

study.what: XP gained is multiplied: level-ups come sooner in every run.
study.note: More levels a run means more cards: it is power, not only pace.

loose_coins.what: A chance on every kill to drop a coin bag: 0.01 = one kill in a hundred.
loose_coins.note: A chance per kill, so it grows with the crowd: keep the numbers small. No bag drops while the Coin Bag power-up is a Trail node not yet bought.

care_package.what: A chance on every kill to drop a cake slice that heals: 0.01 = one kill in a hundred.
care_package.note: A chance per kill: keep the numbers small. No cake drops while the Cake power-up is a Trail node not yet bought.

long_buff.what: A power-up picked up off the ground lasts this much longer (Berserk, Sprint, the Shield).
long_buff.note: Not a structure's buff, Pollen or Barrel Rush.

power_drop.what: Multiplies the chance that a killed creature drops a power-up.
power_drop.note: Only the per-kill drop of the map's timeline; a barrel's throw has its own chance.

reroll.what: One more reroll of the offered cards in every run (an outlaw starts a run with 1).
reroll.note: A whole number. A stage is its own run, so each stage starts with all of them.

skip.what: One more skip of a card offer in every stage (2 at the start).
skip.note: A whole number. With the Assayer's Scale a skip also pays.

banish.what: One more banish in every stage (1 at the start): the banished card is not offered again in that run.

grubstake.what: The purse holds this many coins when a run starts (25 = 25 coins).
grubstake.note: Flat coins, as they are (Greed does not grow them). They are banked with the purse at the run's end, so the node pays itself back over runs; they also count for anything in the run that reads the purse.

spirit.what: Every Totem Pole gift is this much bigger: 0.10 = each offered boost x1.1.
spirit.note: Only the totems' gifts, not how many poles a map has.

bounty.what: A boss chest pays this much more coins and XP: 0.10 = x1.1 on what the chest holds.
bounty.note: Only the boss's chest. Not the Bounty Board's posters, and not the coins creatures drop.

stakes.what: Regular creatures get tougher for good: this much more HP and attack, and 0.4 of it in walking speed (0.10 = +10% HP and attack, +4% speed). An optional node; once bought it cannot be undone.
stakes.note: Designer's note, never told to the player: the same creatures also pay half the number more XP and coins (0.10 = +5%). Bosses and Elites are not touched (that is Boss Stakes).

boss_stakes.what: Bosses and Elites get tougher for good: this much more HP and attack, and 0.4 of it in speed (0.10 = +10% HP and attack, +4% speed). An optional node; once bought it cannot be undone.
boss_stakes.note: Designer's note, never told to the player: bosses and Elites also pay half the number more XP and coins (0.10 = +5%). The regular crowd is not touched (that is Stakes).
